reasoning.Sources: The reproduction report clearly states the research questions and identifies all datasets (ImageNet, Con-text, CUB-200-2011, ACRIMA) as publicly available and straightforward to obtain. This provides sufficient detail to initialize the computational workflow.
reasoning.Methods: While the SCOUTER architecture was easy to understand and code for training models was provided, the reproducers had to implement all explanation evaluation metrics from scratch. The original paper did not provide code for these metrics, nor a complete description of their implementation or all hyperparameters (e.g., 'slots per class'). This required significant reverse-engineering, inference, and implementation, indicating partial specification.
reasoning.Experiments: The report details the computational resources (GPU, training/evaluation times) and general experimental setup. However, the reproducers faced memory allocation issues, had to infer some hyperparameters, and deviated from the original protocol (e.g., single run on ImageNet vs. three independent runs) due to time constraints and missing information. The inability to reproduce results for Con-text and CUB-200-2011, even after trying more epochs, further highlights issues with experimental configurations or undocumented parameters.
reasoning.Sinks: The reproduction report explicitly states a failure to reproduce the main claims. Only 22.2% of explanation evaluation metrics (Claim 1) and 55.5% of classification accuracy scores (Claim 2) were reproducible. While scores for confusion matrix metrics (Claim 3) were reproduced, the report concludes that the original claim of 'higher scores' was not strongly justified by the reproduced values. The tables in the report show numerous non-reproduced scores, indicating that the reported conclusions cannot be traced to reconstructable workflow steps.
